text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Vietnamese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Electricity prices will increase by 50-60 dong per kilowatt hour per year from 1997 to cover increasing costs of power generation.
-- The government has outlined categories of intellectual works which will be covered by a copyright law.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has called for compulsory labour to be used for reforestation programmes.
-- A financial mission from the United States is in Vietnam to discuss debt issues.
-- Benin's Foreign Affairs and Cooperation Minister Pierre Osho has begun a visit to Vietnam to strengthen ties between the two countries and prepare for the 1997 Francophonie summit in Hanoi.
-- Industrial growth reached 13.5 percent in the first two months of 1997.
-- Violations in economic management caused losses of more than $392 million in 1996.
-- Communist Party General Secretary Do Muoi has called for all two million members of the Party to improve their competence and knowledge.
-- A nationwide population census will begin on April 1, the first since 1989.
